1.why: verify-token hashes the submitted code and compares it in constant time only against the recovery bound to the current session via currentRecovery's sessionId check.

2.why: Recoveries are bound to their owning session (recovery.sessionId !== session.id yields a 403), so the same code cannot be used from any other session.

3.why: Nothing invalidates sessions upon reset completion — sessions Map entries persist and only the CSRF token rotates on manual start-over — though the app has no per-account login sessions to invalidate.

4.why: Bun.serve is TLS-only, rejects non-HTTPS request URLs, and sets HSTS, but no explicit TLS version is pinned to confirm the 'latest' version.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as Argon2id hashes with contact data never persisted — hashing rather than encryption, but appropriate one-way protection.

6.why: No real email is sent; the response message is generic and the simulated delivery token is returned only to its owning HTTPS session, so no private user data is exposed in messages.

7.why: All inputs are validated against strict allowlists (validContact, validToken, validMfaCode, strongPassword), JSON bodies are content-type and size checked, and the client renders only via textContent.

8.why: There are no redirects or outgoing links at all — navigation is same-origin hash routing with form-action and connect-src locked to 'self'.

9.why: No email templates exist, all UI and log rendering uses textContent (never innerHTML) under a nonce-based CSP, and user input is never reflected as HTML or script.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the on-page 'Logs' panel deliberately displays the reset token and MFA code, so tokens are in fact shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords (Argon2id) and reset tokens (SHA-256) are stored hashed, but the MFA secret '482913' is hardcoded directly in the source and returned to clients.

12.why: No default login credentials exist, but the hardcoded universal MFA code 482913 works for every recovery, functioning as a default credential.

13.why: Token, password, and MFA attempts are limited to 5 (3 for recovery requests) per window with a 15-minute lockout enforced by checkLimit/recordFailure.

14.why: /api/recovery-request returns the same generic message regardless of contact validity and never persists or looks up the contact, preventing account enumeration.

15.why: The reset code is randomHex(32) (256-bit entropy), stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single-use, expiring after 10 minutes, and bound to the requesting session.
